cues.en: What about... I mean, was was the... Did they hold the boldness against you? Mean, was there a feeling that perhaps the twenty fourth century Well... Which is when this thing is... Right. Yes. That that that came up at the very first press conference. A reporter asked Gene Roddenberry,
cues.zh: 那……我是说，是不是……他们有没有因为你的秃顶对你有意见？我是说，是不是有种感觉，也许到了二十四世纪……嗯……也就是这个故事设定的年代……对。是的。这事在第一次新闻发布会上就提出来了。有位记者问 Gene Roddenberry，

cues.en: look, you know, it doesn't make any sense. You've got a bald actor playing this part. Surely, by the twenty fourth century, they will have found a cure for male pattern baldness.
cues.zh: 你看，这根本说不通。你让一个秃顶演员演这个角色。到了二十四世纪，他们肯定已经找到治疗男性型脱发的方法了。

cues.en: And Gene Roddenberry said, no. By the twenty fourth century, no one will care.
cues.zh: Gene Roddenberry 说，不。到了二十四世纪，没人会在意这个。

cues.en: Oh, good remark. It was, yeah, it was one of the nicest things that's ever been said about men like me. Well, but but but nobody care. You're fashionable now, aren't you? You're in fact a head of fashion. Yeah. And it was nice for a while when I saw all of these shaved heads, but it it began to irritate me, frankly. You know, when somebody has a magnificent head of hair that, honestly, when I was 19, I would have loved to have had. And they shave it all off, and I feel that somehow they're kind of infringing on my territory. Is that is that when you lost your hair at 19? 19. It all happened within the space of a year. It was horrible. It was horrible. I thought everything was over,
cues.zh: 哦，说得好。是啊，这是关于像我这样的人说过的最好的话之一。可是，可是没人会在意。你现在很时尚，不是吗？你其实领先时尚。是啊。有一阵子我看到那么多光头，觉得挺好，但说实话，后来我开始有点恼火。你知道，有些人有一头漂亮的头发，老实说，我19岁时会特别想拥有。可他们全剃光了，我就觉得他们好像在侵犯我的地盘。你19岁开始掉头发，是那时候吗？19岁。一年之内全掉光了。太可怕了。太可怕了。我以为一切都完了，

cues.en: especially,
cues.zh: 尤其是，

cues.en: you know, one aspect of my life. Ladies.
cues.zh: 你知道，我生活的一个方面。女士们。

cues.en: Finished. Was it? Nobody's gonna want... Was it? Over? Yeah. And and that time, not later. I know it wasn't later, but but was it? You
cues.zh: 完了。是吗？没人会想要……是吗？结束了？对。而且是那时候，不是后来。我知道不是后来，但当时是不是？你

cues.en: know nothing, Michael. You know? You're making it up. No. It actually wasn't,
cues.zh: 什么都不知道，Michael。你知道吗？你在瞎编。不。其实不是，

cues.en: but I I felt I was inhibited by it. Yeah. I I I would have been bolder
cues.zh: 但我……我觉得自己因此受到了束缚。是的。我……我本来会更胆大

cues.en: in my relationship with young women than I was.
cues.zh: 在和年轻女性交往时，比我当时更胆大。

cues.en: It was probably all for the best of Absolutely. I think we should be circumspect when we're 19, but had lots of problems. But did you have a flap, didn't you? The old Bobby Charles? Yes, I did.
cues.zh: 那大概都是最好的安排，绝对是。我觉得19岁时我们应该谨慎些，但当时有很多问题。不过你戴过假发，对吧？老 Bobby Charles 那种？是的，我戴过。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: and I I wear... Wore hats all the time. Yeah. Caps, especially if it was windy because, know, the thing would happen. And that was always so silly about Bobby, wasn't it? I mean, the worst possible job he had for having one of those shows.
cues.zh: 而且我一直……一直戴帽子。是啊，尤其刮风的时候戴鸭舌帽，因为你知道，那玩意儿会出状况。Bobby 这点总是很傻，不是吗？我是说，他做那种节目，却干着最糟糕不过的活儿。

cues.en: Shall I tell you how I lost it? Yeah.
cues.zh: 要我讲讲我是怎么把它弄丢的吗？好啊。

cues.en: I... There was a man who had been at school with me at drama school,
cues.zh: 我……有个人以前和我在戏剧学校同过学，

cues.en: Hungarian. He was older than the rest of us. He'd run his own theater in Budapest. He came out in '56.
cues.zh: 匈牙利人。他比我们其他人都年长。他在布达佩斯经营过自己的剧院。他是56年出来的。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: he he was a man of strong personality and and a good loyal friend to me. He was also a judo black belt. He was very short and very powerful. He invited me, and his wife invited me for lunch one day. And we had lunch. It was very nice, bottle of wine. And the two of them got up at the end of of the lunch, and I thought they were gonna make coffee or something. And all of a sudden, I was grabbed from behind by George,
cues.zh: 他他个性很强，而且……而且对我来说是个忠诚的好朋友。他还是柔道黑带。他个子很矮，但非常强壮。有一天他和他妻子邀请我去吃午饭。我们吃了午饭，很不错，还喝了一瓶葡萄酒。午饭结束时，他们俩站了起来，我以为他们要去煮咖啡什么的。突然，我被 George 从后面抓住了，

cues.en: this big powerful man. And he... I thought he was playing some kind of game, so I was laughing and joking. And then his wife appeared in front of me with a pair of scissors.
cues.zh: 这个高大强壮的男人。他……我以为他在玩什么游戏，所以我又笑又开玩笑。然后他妻子拿着一把剪刀出现在我面前。

cues.en: And and I knew in an instant what she was going to do, and I began to scream and shout. And now it was serious. I was fighting. I mean, I was fighting to keep my appearance, and she lifted it up, and she cut it all off. And then George, he worked his way, still holding me, came around, and he knelt down in front me and he said, now you be yourself.
cues.zh: 而且……而且我一下子就明白她要干什么，我开始尖叫大喊。这下可严重了。我在挣扎。我是说，我在为保住自己的样子而挣扎，她把那东西往上一提，全剪掉了。然后 George 还抱着我，慢慢绕到前面，在我面前跪下，说：现在做你自己吧。

cues.en: No more hiding. And he was right because I used to walk like this.
cues.zh: 不再遮掩了。他说得对，因为我以前走路是这样的。

cues.en: You know, because I was embarrassed about this thing and so I couldn't stand up properly. You know, it was it was not only inhibiting as a person. It was hopeless if you're an actor, of course. Yes. You Because So you have to wear a toupee, do I did. Yes. I I never wore one socially.
cues.zh: 你知道，因为我对这件事感到难为情，所以没法好好站直。你知道，这不仅是作为一个人受到束缚。当然，如果你是演员，那更是没戏了。是的。你因为所以你得戴假发，我戴了。是的。我私下从来不戴。

cues.en: Yes. But I used to wear it when I went up for jobs.
cues.zh: 是的。但我以前去面试工作时会戴。

cues.en: The one occasion that it rebounded on me, I got an audition for the National Theatre for Laurence Olivier,
cues.zh: 唯一一次让我栽跟头的是，我得到了国家剧院为劳伦斯·奥利弗选角的试镜机会，

cues.en: and I went down to their
cues.zh: 我去了他们在

cues.en: their little setup there they had down at The Cut in Waterloo.
cues.zh: 他们在滑铁卢The Cut那里的一个小场地。

cues.en: And I did what I was in. I wore the toupee
cues.zh: 我到了之后，我戴了假发

cues.en: to the audition so I could put it on myself. It was really good. It looked entirely natural.
cues.zh: 去试镜，这样我可以自己戴上。效果真的很好。看起来完全自然。

cues.en: And I went in, and I did my first piece with the toupee,
cues.zh: 我走进去，戴着假发演了第一段，

cues.en: and and he was sitting there right in front of me. And it was a nerve wracking experience. You can imagine it, you know, young actor.
cues.zh: 他就坐在我正前方。那真是让人紧张的经历。你可以想象，你知道，年轻演员。

cues.en: And I finished it, and I I started to explain what my second piece would be. And as I did that, I started doing this, you see,
cues.zh: 我演完了，然后我开始解释我第二段要演什么。就在我说话的时候，我开始做这个动作，你看，

cues.en: with my fingers. And I'm talking to him all the time, and I unclip from the back, and I take it off, and I put it down on the chib side of me, and I start my second piece. Well, I can see immediately that I haven't got his attention. He's
cues.zh: 用我的手指。我一直跟他说话，然后我从后面解开夹子，把假发摘下来，放在我旁边的椅子上，然后开始演第二段。好吧，我立刻就看出来，我没能抓住他的注意力。他

cues.en: he's looking down here
cues.zh: 他正往下看这里

cues.en: like this. And when I finished, he
cues.zh: 像这样。等我演完，他

cues.en: said,
cues.zh: 说，

cues.en: do it again.
cues.zh: 再来一遍。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: I said, you you want me to do one of the pieces again? He said, no. No. No. Take that off and do it again. Put it on and take it off. And and I did, and he said, marvelous. That's marvelous.
cues.zh: 我说，你、你想让我把其中一段再演一遍吗？他说，不。不。不。脱下来再演一遍。穿上再脱下来。我照做了，他说，太棒了。这太棒了。

cues.en: And I swear it was the only thing about my audition he remembered.
cues.zh: 我发誓这是他对我试镜唯一记住的事情。

cues.en: So there's always a story in a way in case sometime he had to do I waited for the moment in one of his performances when he would do something like that. But, you know, those days are now past, and I can relish what I have.
cues.zh: 所以总有这样一个故事，以防有朝一日他不得不……我在他的一场表演中等待着那个时刻，那时他会做出那样的举动。但是，你知道，那些日子已经过去了，我可以细细品味我所拥有的。
